question: Should OpenClaw accept the signed hosted marketplace feed trust stack in core now, including config trust anchors, snapshot trust columns, verifier behavior, and CLI trust disclosure?
rationale: The code path is coherent and has real CLI proof, but it changes compatibility and security-boundary behavior that needs maintainer signoff, and the prerequisite stack is still open.

options.title: Review and land the stack in order
options.body: Keep this PR open, finish the prerequisite verifier, config, and refresh-state PRs first, then re-review this CLI visibility slice after rebase.

options.title: Narrow to the top CLI slice
options.body: Ask the contributor to rebase after prerequisites land so this branch carries only trust-state output and diagnostics.

options.title: Pause the signed-feed direction
options.body: Leave the stack unmerged or close it if maintainers decide hosted feed signatures should not be a core marketplace responsibility yet.

recommendation.title: Review and land the stack in order
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open, finish the prerequisite verifier, config, and refresh-state PRs first, then re-review this CLI visibility slice after rebase.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the best available maintainer-side owner for deciding whether this security-boundary stack belongs in core now.
